oneliner.t: Birmingham criminal-defense and estate attorney and former Midfield municipal judge who won the 2026 Democratic runoff for Alabama's open U.S. Senate seat and faces Republican Rep. Barry Moore on Nov. 3.

upbringing.t: The public record says little about his early life. He says he has lived in Alabama since 1979, living at various points in Huntsville, Birmingham, Selma and the Mobile area. A 2016 candidate profile lists an associate degree from Selma University in 1981, followed by a computer science/mathematics bachelor's from Alabama A&M in 1985. He says he paid for college in part with a Pell Grant. He worked about a decade in software in Huntsville, then moved to Birmingham, where he earned a law degree in 2000.

career.role: Software analyst (says work included NASA payload software and Army Patriot missile systems)
Lead defense attorney for Harvey Updyke (Toomer's Corner tree-poisoning case)

platform.t: Direct federal money to rural hospitals and emergency departments, recruit physicians and medical staff, and make prescription drugs and care more affordable; also lists veterans' health care as a priority.
Campaigned on raising the federal minimum wage; blames the Trump administration for high gas, grocery and prescription prices, which he ties to the Iran war.
Opposes the budget reconciliation law for shifting SNAP costs to states and for not extending enhanced ACA premium tax credits.
Opposes the Trump proclamation expanding foreign beef imports, backs Rep. Shomari Figures' bill to nullify it, and wants wider scrutiny of tariff policy with input from Alabama farmers.
Wants to restore stability for federal workers (citing DOGE-linked cuts at Redstone Arsenal and the VA) and protect federal research funding at UAB, Alabama A&M, Auburn and Tuskegee.
Protect federal student loan and Pell Grant programs; supports quality public education.

Says Supreme Court decisions and redistricting raise constitutional questions Congress must address, citing immigration enforcement and family separations; lists voting rights, equal justice and 'safe communities' as priorities.
Says he wants to lower the temperature in Congress and work across party lines, and would work closely with Reps. Terri Sewell and Shomari Figures.

promises.t: Steer federal funding to rural hospitals, strengthen emergency departments, and recruit doctors and medical staff to Alabama.
Support Rep. Shomari Figures' bill to nullify the beef-import proclamation and bar waivers of beef import duties without congressional approval.
Protect federal student loan and Pell Grant programs.
Restore stability to federal employment, including at Redstone Arsenal and the VA.

checks.legal: Courts: CourtListener (courtlistener.com/?q="Everett Wess") and Justia searches were tried directly and were blocked for this research tool, so courts are 'news': news archives, Bhamwiki and BirminghamWatch. No case naming Wess as a party was found. Cases he handled as defense counsel (e.g., Harvey Updyke, 2011–2012) are not his legal record. Alacourt is paywalled and was not searched. Ethics: as a former municipal judge he falls under the Alabama Judicial Inquiry Commission; its public press-release page was checked directly (one release, 2023, about a different judge), and Wess is not named. Alabama State Bar discipline was not searched directly; Avvo, which draws on bar data, reports 'No misconduct found' with license status 'Authorized to Practice' since 2000.
checks.foreign: FARA: reached efile.fara.gov, but its name search is an interactive form the tool cannot submit, and the bulk files are zipped binaries it cannot read, so no FARA name search was completed ('no'). Senate eFD was tried and the access request went unanswered. News searches found no foreign business or government ties.
checks.claims: Mechanical v2.1 sample: (a) every checkable claim in the bio section of wessforsenate.com, a single-page site (15 rated); (b) the issues section lists three pillars (Safe Communities, Affordable Healthcare, Protecting Your Rights), which are position statements with no checkable facts; (c) no Wess campaign ads were found in news or search, so none were sampled. Earlier claims from the Spectrum News interview (only lawyer in the field; Sweetser's Trump votes; Irondale 'prosecutor'; NASA/Patriot software; in Alabama since 1979) fall outside the mechanical sample and were dropped.
checks.democracy: Never held an office that voted on certification. Searched news coverage for statements on the 2020 and 2024 results, Jan. 6 or certification; none found.

recordx.note: No officeholder vote record (never in Congress). disclosure is unknown: efdsearch.senate.gov was tried once and the access request went unanswered, and no reporting on his Senate candidate disclosure was found. fec is unknown: the earlier 'clean' was removed because the FEC committee filings/RFAI tab loads by script and showed no rows, the same limit that applied to Moore.

research_notes: NOMINATION CONFIRMED: Wess placed first in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary (132,373 votes, 39.8%, per Wikipedia; APR reported 39.6%) ahead of Dakarai Larriett (28.9%), Mark Wheeler II (17.4%) and Kyle Sweetser (13.9%). He won the June 16 runoff over Larriett, with about 54.6–54.7% (Wikipedia: 49,396 to 41,065; BirminghamWatch: 50,229 to 41,779; Reflector election night: 48,996 to 40,589). AP called the race for him. The Alabama SOS certified canvass was not fetched; confirm final runoff totals there. MONEY: The FEC figures are from the candidate/committee summary covering Jan. 1–June 30, 2026: $80,554.63 receipts, of which $70,643.23 was candidate loans and $9,911.40 was individual contributions; $18,282.65 cash on hand; $70,643.23 debts. The Q3 report (due Oct. 15) is not yet filed. CONFLICTS: the Reflector (Sept. 25) said he raised 'slightly less than $4,000' through end of June, perhaps meaning contributions only in one period. Wikipedia's table shows $83,341 raised, $94,747 spent and $0 cash on hand as of June 30, which does not match the FEC summary. FEC itemized receipts, filings list, quarterly breakdown, top donors and industries could not be fetched (robots-blocked). OpenSecrets was blocked. No outside spending for or against Wess was found; reported outside spending in the race (e.g., crypto PAC Fairshake about $5M) backed Moore in the GOP primary. ISRAEL: No AIPAC endorsement, pro-Israel PAC money, UDP spending or Israel/Gaza statements found. The FEC summary shows $0 from PACs, so no AIPAC PAC earmarks are indicated, but itemized earmarks could not be verified. OFFICE: He held an appointed municipal judgeship (Midfield) and was appointed special circuit/district judge in Jefferson County, per his own questionnaires; dates are not documented, so office_years is omitted. He has never held elected office. PRIOR CAMPAIGNS (all lost): 2013 Birmingham City Council District 2 (5th of 6); 2014 Jefferson County Circuit Court Place 3 Dem primary (42.2%); 2016 10th Circuit Place 26 Dem runoff (46.6%); 2018 Probate Judge Place 1 Dem primary (42.7%); 2020 10th Circuit Place 3 Dem primary (21.2%); 2024 Probate Judge Dem primary (19.9%, 3rd). Sources: Ballotpedia, Bhamwiki, BirminghamWatch. No specific promises were documented for those races (BirminghamWatch 2018 says 'Main issues: information not available'), so promises_prev is empty. In 2020 he lent his own campaign $29,622.82 (BirminghamWatch). DEBATES: No general-election debate is scheduled as of Oct. 1. Independent Craig Jelks challenged Wess and Moore to debate; neither campaign responded to APR. Jelks also urged Wess to quit (Sept. 10); Wess's campaign declined comment. Wess's participation in Democratic primary forums (e.g., Franklin County Democrats) was not verified. Debate counts are recorded as 0/0, meaning no debate was documented, not that he declined one. GAPS: birthplace and hometown not documented. Bhamwiki says he attended Moss Point High School in Mississippi (single source; omitted). MBA year is 1995 in three sources, 1996 in WBHM 2016. His law firm start is 2000 in questionnaires, 2001 on the site. No photo found on Wikimedia Commons. No Senate financial disclosure was found. No legal, ethics, lien or business-closure records were found, but Alacourt, PACER and the State Bar database were not searched directly. Needs a human check. v2.1 UPDATE (2026-10-08): Re-checked the FEC candidate page (only the 2026 cycle; figures unchanged through 2026-06-30, $0 from PACs). Track AIPAC's congress list does not include him. No super PAC spending for or against him was found, so money_flags = {}. Avvo lists his full name as Everett Warkeen Wess. The Alabama Judicial Inquiry Commission's site posts only one public press release (2023), so the absence of complaints there is weak evidence. 'Juris Doctor' and A&M degrees are confirmed by the Alabama Reflector's candidate profile and Bhamwiki; the Reflector does not give its source.
